ptn.reference_statement: Существующий порядок оплаты и социальных гарантий работников нефтегазового сектора является приемлемым и не требует существенного изменения.

source_bias_warning: The source is openly hostile toward the dismissed workers. Loaded descriptions, insults, motive claims, and the author's normative judgments are not evidence of actor POS/KVS. Only specific attributed demands, actions, offers, refusals and pay-treatment statements may be coded.

actors.actor_scope: Dismissed/former OMG workers and their representatives in the 23-24 November negotiation episode as attributed in the archived article.
coder_visible_evidence: The source states that the dismissed workers wanted to return to OMG and sought higher pay treatment involving the 1.7 and 1.8 coefficients.
The article says a subsequent meeting took place on 23-24 November with invited worker-side representatives and experts.
It reports that the dismissed workers rejected the proposed settlement/compromise and did not sign the reconciliation document.
It reports that removal of the OMG director was also among the demands, so pay was not the only issue.
actors.limited_exact_fragment: Они желают… ну, вы уже догадались – вернуться в ОМГ и умножить свои бывшие оклады на 1.7. и 1.8.

actors.actor_scope: RD KMG / OMG employer-side position and actions in the same meeting episode, excluding actions attributable only to government authorities.
coder_visible_evidence: The source describes the employer-side position that the disputed coefficients had already been incorporated in pay calculations and that additional reimbursement or a further salary increase on that basis was not accepted.

The article reports that RD KMG had revised its contractor-use plan to support alternative jobs and had a multi-year arrangement creating additional contractor positions; this employment offer is context and must not be treated as pay-specific KVS unless the rubric predicate is met.

The article reports willingness in the negotiation context to revisit some collective-agreement provisions, but the source often merges government and employer actions. If employer attribution for a decisive predicate is not clear, C4 must fail.
The source states that the employer/administrative side defended the legality/correctness of the existing coefficient treatment.

dependency_limits: Both actor rows come from the same archived article and are not independent corroboration.
No current-only later republication is decisive evidence in this input.
The article is a mediated report of the meeting, not the meeting protocol itself.
